title: Precision-swap warmstart batcher: long-tail latency & throughput matrix
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Investigate how dynamic precision switching (FP8 <-> INT8) and warmstart behavior for KV cache interact with the continuous batching layer under long-context workloads. Goal is to produce a throughput vs. tail-latency matrix across representative prompt mixes and to document accuracy regressions introduced by precision-swap and warmstart transitions.
goal: Deliver a repeatable benchmark suite and runbook that measures end-to-end impact of precision swaps and KV-warmstart across batching strategies for sequences up to 32k tokens. Provide regression-safe config recommendations for production runtime to avoid tail-latency spikes when switching quantized variants.
success_metrics: p50/p95/p99 token latency delta vs float32 baseline
sustained throughput (tokens/sec) for mixed sequence-length traffic
fraction of requests experiencing fallback kernel invocations
accuracy regression on validation prompts: < 0.8% LLR drop and < 0.5% perplexity increase
KV warmstart hit-rate and warmup cost measured in added tokens and ms
approach: Define traffic mixes (short/medium/long, synthetic and sampled prod anonymized prompts)
Implement orchestration to perform precision-swap at request-granularity and at model-instance-granularity in Dedicated cluster
Measure KV cache warmstart penalties when a request transitions between precision modes and when model variant is swapped in a serving pool
Sweep batching window sizes and microbatch shapes (e.g., fixed-batch, continuous-batcher with latency SLO knobs)
Record kernel fallback counts, memory pressure events, and quantization-related numeric warnings
benchmark_plan: 1) Baseline runs: float32 and fp16 serving with standard batching; collect p50/p95/p99 and throughput
2) FP8 and INT8 variants: calibrated profiles applied, run with identical batching to baseline
3) Precision-swap scenarios: a) per-request swap (dispatcher-level), b) per-instance swap (rolling deploy)
4) Warmstart test: schedule swaps in hot path to observe KV cache cold/start churn and measure token latency overhead
5) Batching interaction grid: batch sizes [1,4,8,32,128], continuous-batcher latency targets [5ms, 20ms, 50ms], and long-context windows [2k,8k,32k]
6) Accuracy validation: run eval suite (LAMBADA variant, targeted prompt set, and embedding cosine similarity) before/after swaps
7) Stability runs: 6-hour soak with synthetic bursty traffic to catch microburst-induced tail regressions
datasets: embedding-stability-set (1k pairs for cosine delta checks)
rigs: control-plane: staging-console + tracing collector (jaeger) + perf dashboards (grafana)
steps: Add precision-swap orchestration to harness and unit-test the dispatcher behavior
Publish calibrated FP8 and INT8 profiles for model-v2.3 to artifact storage and reference them in runs
Run baseline float/FP16 runs across the batching grid and record metrics to perf-gcs-bucket
Execute precision-swap scenarios and collect traces, kernel fallback counts, and KV warmstart spans
Run accuracy eval suite and produce per-prompt delta CSVs
Aggregate results, produce throughput/latency matrix, and draft runbook with recommended configs
risks: Calibration profiles may not be strictly compatible across kernel implementations causing spurious fallbacks
KV warmstart cost might be higher on Hopper due to allocator behavior; could be misattributed to quantization
Soak runs expose rare OOM/failure modes in continuous-batcher when precision changes increase transient memory
Accuracy metric thresholds may need to be model-family specific; a global threshold risks false-positive failures
